The everyday reality

Eating better shouldn't feel so complicated.

Most people already know roughly what healthier eating looks like. What's usually missing is a way to do it on a normal Tuesday.

01

Balanced meals are vague

You know a plate should be "balanced", but not what that actually means when you're standing in front of the fridge at seven o'clock.

02

The advice contradicts itself

One source says fruit is sugar, the next says breakfast is essential, the next says skip it. None of it was written for your week.

03

Routines don't stick

A strict plan survives nine good days, then meets a week that doesn't cooperate and gets abandoned entirely.

04

Deciding takes too long

Working out what to eat, what to buy and what to cook costs more time and attention than the cooking itself.

This guide is built to give you practical structure — not another strict set of rules to follow perfectly or abandon.

The guide

A clearer way to approach everyday eating.

The Everyday Eating Blueprint is a 47-page PDF that turns healthy eating into a small number of repeatable decisions you can apply to the food you already buy.

Something to refer back to

One organised resource with a clickable contents page and bookmarks, instead of scattered advice you have to search for again each time.

Guidance for real decisions

How to build a plate, what to keep in the house, how to plan a week in about ten minutes, and what to do on the days when the plan falls apart.

Consistency over perfection

No calorie targets, no macro prescriptions and no foods to eliminate. The approach is built to survive a bad week rather than demand a perfect one.

Contents

Everything you need to get started.

Five parts, 47 pages. Here is exactly what is in the guide.

I

The foundations

Five practical principles, the balanced-plate framework, and six worked meal examples — three with meat or fish, three without.

II

Protein & fibre

What they do, which everyday foods contain them, and two reference tables with portions and approximate amounts, sourced from published composition data.

III

Portions & satisfaction

How to judge a portion without weighing anything, and what to change when a meal leaves you hungry an hour later.

IV

Carbs, fats & flexibility

Why bread, pasta and potatoes stay on the plate, how fat carries flavour, and how favourite foods fit into a normal week.

V

Shopping & planning

A seven-category grocery system, a 58-item master checklist, and a ten-minute weekly planning method built around four dinners, not seven.

VI

A seven-day example

An illustrative week of breakfasts, lunches, dinners and snacks showing how leftovers and overlapping ingredients fit together. Vegetarian swaps throughout.

VII

Real-life chapters

Eating well on a budget, healthy eating when you're busy, eating out and social occasions, and food preparation that is actually worth the time.

VIII

18 recipes & ideas

Four breakfasts, four lunches, four dinners, five quick meals and eight snacks — each with real quantities, timings, substitutions and storage notes.

IX

5 fillable worksheets

Build-your-own-meal, a weekly meal planner, a grocery planner, a seven-day habit reset and a habit tracker. Type into them or print them.

X

Troubleshooting & FAQ

Eight common mistakes with practical corrections, ten real-life problems answered, and a frequently-asked-questions section.

XI

Quick-reference cheat sheet

The whole system on one page: the meal formula, protein and fibre foods, carbohydrate options, flavour additions and six fast meals.

XII

Sources

Every numerical claim traced to one of ten cited sources, including the WHO, EFSA, Harvard's Nutrition Source, Mayo Clinic and FoodSafety.gov.

Questions

Before you buy.

What will I receive after purchasing?

One file: The Everyday Eating Blueprint, a 47-page PDF. Nothing else is included — no subscription, no course and no upsell.

Payment is handled by Lemon Squeezy. As soon as it goes through you get a download link on the confirmation page and a copy by email, so you can save the file straight away.

Lemon Squeezy is the merchant of record for the sale, so the receipt comes from them and they handle any sales tax or VAT that applies where you live.

Is this a physical book?

No. It is a digital PDF download. Nothing is printed, posted or shipped. You can print it yourself if you prefer to read on paper — the worksheets are designed to work both on screen and printed.

Can I read it on my phone or tablet?

Yes. It is a standard PDF and opens in the PDF readers built into phones, tablets, laptops and browsers. It is laid out at A4 with text sized for comfortable reading on a screen.

The fillable worksheet fields are standard PDF form fields. They work in most desktop PDF readers; support on mobile readers varies, so on a phone you may prefer to read the guide and print the worksheets.

Is this a personalised nutrition plan?

No. It is a general educational guide for healthy adults. It cannot account for your medical history, medications, allergies, cultural or religious requirements, budget or schedule.

If you have a medical condition, a prescribed or restricted diet, a food allergy, a history of disordered eating, or you are pregnant or breastfeeding, please seek advice from a doctor, registered dietitian or other suitably qualified professional.

Does it tell me to count calories or cut out foods?

No. There are no calorie targets, no macronutrient prescriptions and no forbidden foods in the guide. It works through meal composition, portion awareness and practical planning instead.

Where do the nutrition figures come from?

Every numerical claim is traced to one of ten cited sources, listed on page 46 with working links. The fibre table reproduces values published by the Mayo Clinic, drawn from the USDA National Nutrient Database. The protein values are approximate and cross-checked across published composition tables, and are labelled as such.

Which currency will I be charged in?

The guide is priced in US dollars, and that is what you are charged wherever you are. The amount shown on this page is the amount the checkout bills — your bank or card handles the conversion at its own rate if you hold another currency.

Can I request a refund?

To configure Lemon Squeezy processes the payment and can issue refunds, but the policy is yours to set and must be stated here before you take real orders. Note that buyers in the EU and UK normally have a 14-day right of withdrawal on digital content, which can only be waived if the buyer expressly consents at checkout — Lemon Squeezy has a setting for that.
